title: BACE: Applied Mathematics - BACE - Applied Mathematics - Molarity
subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct definition of **Molarity (M)**?
options: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent
Grams of solute per liter of solution
Moles of solute per liter of solution
Milliliters of solute per 100 mL of solution
questions.explain: Molarity (M) is defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved in one liter of total solution ($mol/L$).
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: The molecular weight of NaCl is **58.44 g/mol**. How much NaCl is required to make **500 mL** of a **0.5 M** solution?
questions.explain: First calculate moles needed for 0.5 L (500 mL) at 0.5 M: $$\text{Moles} = M \times L = 0.5 \text{ mol/L} \times 0.5 \text{ L} = 0.25 \text{ moles}$$ Then convert moles to grams: $$\text{Mass} = \text{Moles} \times \text{MW} = 0.25 \text{ mol} \times 58.44 \text{ g/mol} = 14.61 \text{ g}$$
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: If you have **200 mL** of a **2 M** NaOH solution, how many **moles** of NaOH are present?
questions.explain: First, convert volume to liters: $200 \text{ mL} = 0.2 \text{ L}$. Then use the formula: $$\text{Moles} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (L)}$$ ​$$\text{Moles} = 2 \text{ mol/L} \times 0.2 \text{ L} = 0.4 \text{ moles}$$

questions.q: What is the concentration of H$^+$ ions in a solution with a pH of 3? (Hint: $pH = -\log[H^+]$)
questions.explain: Since $pH = -\log[H^+]$, then $[H^+] = 10^{-pH}$. Therefore, $[H^+] = 10^{-3} \text{ M}$ or $0.001 \text{ M}$.
